To print text and variables in Python, you can use the `print()` function in several ways:

## 1. Printing Simple Text
```python
print("Hello, World!")
# Output: Hello, World!
```

## 2. Printing Variables
```python
name = "Alice"
age = 25
print(name)
print(age)
# Output: Alice
# Output: 25
```

## 3. Printing Multiple Items
```python
print("Name:", name, "Age:", age)
# Output: Name: Alice Age: 25
```

## 4. Using String Concatenation
```python
message = "My name is " + name
print(message)
# Output: My name is Alice
```

## 5. Using f-strings (Formatted String Literals)
```python
print(f"My name is {name} and I am {age} years old")
# Output: My name is Alice and I am 25 years old
```

## 6. Using .format() Method
```python
print("My name is {} and I am {} years old".format(name, age))
# Output: My name is Alice and I am 25 years old
```

## 7. Using % Formatting (Older Method)
```python
print("My name is %s and I am %d years old" % (name, age))
# Output: My name is Alice and I am 25 years old
```

## 8. Printing with Custom Separators
```python
print("Apple", "Banana", "Orange", sep=", ")
# Output: Apple, Banana, Orange
```

## 9. Printing with Custom End Characters
```python
print("Hello", end=" ")
print("World")
# Output: Hello World
```

## 10. Printing Different Data Types
```python
number = 42
pi = 3.14159
is_valid = True
my_list = [1, 2, 3]

print(f"Integer: {number}, Float: {pi}, Boolean: {is_valid}, List: {my_list}")
# Output: Integer: 42, Float: 3.14159, Boolean: True, List: [1, 2, 3]
```
